fact: UNCDF's November 2023 diagnostic says a new regulation on digital financial consumer protection, revising the one in force in Gabon since 2011, is expected, and that CEMAC mediation regulations are nearly finalised in most member countries but still need approval in each.
system: Gabon financial consumer protection regulation (2011, under revision)

fact: UNCTAD's peer-review overview says CEMAC Regulation No. 04/18/CEMAC/UMAC/COBAC of 21 December 2018 on payment services, directly applicable in Gabon, protects consumers' funds, which may be used only for payment operations and are shielded from other creditors.

UNCTAD's peer-review overview says CEMAC Regulation No. 01/20/CEMAC/UMAC/COBAC of 3 July 2020 on banking products and services, directly applicable in Gabon, requires banks to publish conditions, bans misleading advertising and organises amicable handling of consumer complaints.
system: CEMAC Regulation 01/20 on banking products and services

fact: UNCTAD's peer-review overview says a 2022 draft consumer protection law, covering financial and banking services and electronic communication services, is pending, Gabon having no specific consumer protection law and the 2019 CEMAC directive not yet transposed.

CEMAC Regulation 01/20 of 3 July 2020 on consumer protection for banking products and services, with a Prime Minister's decree of 21 March 2024 and two ministerial arrets of 7 January 2025, sets the financial mediation framework, covering payment institutions and mobile money disputes.
